_see: references/harness-portability.md — the capability/evidence contract this file is checked against by scripts/check-harnesses.sh.

statuses.Verified: Discovery, non-interactive invocation, AND at least one end-to-end wgm journey are recorded as evidence objects with references. No entry may be Verified without them.
statuses.Expected: The harness fits the contract on documented evidence (skill discovery and a non-interactive mode are published by the vendor), but no wgm journey has been run and recorded. Expected is a prediction, not a claim.
statuses.Degraded: wgm runs, but a named host capability is missing. The entry must name the missing capability and the fallback wgm uses without it.
statuses.Unknown: No reliable evidence either way. Unknown entries carry no evidence objects; sources may still record what a vendor documents.

harnesses.name: Pi

skill_discovery.notes: Pi implements the Agent Skills standard natively and reads ~/.agents/skills/, which is exactly where scripts/install.sh puts wgm — so no Pi-specific install step is expected. Documented in Pi's README; not yet executed by wgm.

invocation.notes: Pi's README documents print mode (-p/--print), JSON-lines mode (--mode json), and RPC mode (--mode rpc). wgm has never executed scripts/loop.sh against pi, so the headless details here are documented-not-executed and the exact flag set may drift.

subagents.notes: Pi's README states it deliberately ships without sub agents and plan mode, and expects such workflows to come from extensions or third-party pi packages.

harnesses.missing_capability: Host-dispatched subagents — the two-stage role swarm and the five-role docs-audit swarm have no host primitive to launch.
harnesses.fallback: Run the two review passes and the docs-audit personas inline and sequentially in one context, as references/subagents.md's no-subagent fallback prescribes, and record the dissent explicitly. The portable kernel (grill, plan, loop, deterministic gates) is unaffected.

adapter.notes: A Pi extension or pi package could dispatch role subagents; none is written. Until one exists, Pi runs the portable kernel only.

os_evidence.windows: unverified — Pi documents Windows and Termux setup; no recorded wgm run

harnesses.notes: Next real dogfood target. Running one full wgm journey under Pi is what would move discovery and invocation to verified; the missing subagent primitive keeps the entry Degraded regardless, until a Pi adapter exists.

harnesses.name: GitHub Copilot CLI

skill_discovery.notes: scripts/install.sh installs into ~/.copilot/skills/wgm (client target, evidenced by the installer source and wgm's published install docs) and into the shared ~/.agents/skills/wgm, which is the layout scripts/test-install.sh asserts on every run.

invocation.notes: Published as wgm's reference non-interactive contract in docs/reference/cli-loop.md and used by scripts/loop.sh; the permission flag is required for unattended tool use.

subagents.notes: The twelve role agents in .github/agents/*.agent.md are launched by the host dispatcher; the portable runner never claims to launch them itself.

harnesses.fallback: If the host session cannot dispatch custom agents, run both review passes and the docs-audit personas inline and sequentially, preserving dissent.

adapter.notes: wgm ships the host-format role agents this harness dispatches (.github/agents/*.agent.md), checked structurally by scripts/check-docs.sh.

os_evidence.linux: verified — wgm's own development, loop, and docs-audit runs execute here
os_evidence.windows: unverified — native-Windows runs are not recorded; the WSL mirror of the shared ~/.agents layout is exercised by scripts/test-install.sh

evidence.detail: scripts/test-install.sh asserts the shared ~/.agents/skills/wgm layout (install, idempotent re-run, uninstall, WSL mirror, companions) that Copilot CLI also reads; the ~/.copilot/skills/wgm client target is evidenced by the installer source and the published install docs, not by that harness.
`copilot -p --allow-all-tools` is the published non-interactive contract the loop runs unattended.

This repository's own grill → plan → loop → review → docs-audit journeys were driven from Copilot CLI, and the audits are committed as a paper trail. Copilot-Session trailers appear in the history from 2026-07-30 onward — 22 of 179 commits as counted on 2026-08-24, not every commit and not every commit since that date — so the trailers corroborate the journeys rather than enumerate them.

harnesses.notes: The only harness with all three evidence tiers on record. macOS and native Windows remain unverified even here — Verified is per-contract, not per-platform.

harnesses.name: Claude Code

skill_discovery.notes: Anthropic documents personal and project skill directories; scripts/install.sh targets ~/.claude/skills/wgm when that directory exists.

invocation.notes: Headless mode is documented by the vendor and published in wgm's docs; no recorded wgm run pins the flag set.

subagents.notes: Claude Code documents subagents, but wgm ships no Claude-format agent definitions, so the role swarm runs inline unless the operator authors them.

harnesses.fallback: Inline sequential two-pass review per references/subagents.md when no host-format agent definitions are installed.

adapter.notes: Translating .github/agents/*.agent.md into Claude subagent definitions is unwritten work.

harnesses.notes: wgm's docs have long listed this harness as known-good, but the repository holds no recorded end-to-end journey, so the contract rates it Expected. Promoting it needs one recorded run, not a stronger adjective.

harnesses.name: OpenAI Codex CLI

skill_discovery.notes: OpenAI documents repo-, user-, admin-, and system-scoped skills; the user scope is ~/.agents/skills, which scripts/install.sh already writes.

invocation.notes: wgm's docs publish `codex exec`; sandbox and approval flags vary by version and are deliberately not pinned here.

subagents.notes: Third-party claims that Codex CLI exposes a dispatchable subagent primitive are not corroborated by OpenAI's skills documentation; treat Codex subagent capability as unverified.

harnesses.fallback: Inline sequential two-pass review per references/subagents.md; assume no host subagent dispatch until it is corroborated.

adapter.notes: No Codex-format role definitions ship with wgm.

harnesses.notes: Skill discovery is the strongest documented fit after Copilot CLI; the unverified part is subagent dispatch, not loading the skill.

harnesses.name: Gemini CLI

skill_discovery.notes: Gemini CLI documents user and workspace skills and treats .agents/skills as an interoperable alias that takes precedence over .gemini/skills.

invocation.notes: Headless mode is documented by the vendor; wgm has no recorded run, so approval/tool flags for unattended use are unverified.

subagents.notes: No subagent primitive wgm can dispatch was corroborated in the vendor CLI documentation.

harnesses.fallback: Inline sequential two-pass review per references/subagents.md.

adapter.notes: No Gemini-format role definitions ship with wgm.

harnesses.notes: Contract-fit on documentation alone. Nothing here has been executed by wgm.

harnesses.name: Cursor CLI

skill_discovery.notes: Cursor documents Agent Skills discovery from project and user directories, and additionally loads Claude- and Codex-compatible skill directories.

invocation.notes: Cursor's CLI binary is `agent`; print mode is documented for scripts and CI. Model and output-format flags are version-dependent and not pinned here.

subagents.notes: Cursor documents custom subagents, but wgm ships no Cursor-format subagent definitions, so the role swarm runs inline.

harnesses.fallback: Inline sequential two-pass review per references/subagents.md.

adapter.notes: A Cursor-format translation of .github/agents/*.agent.md is unwritten work.

harnesses.notes: Documented fit for both discovery and headless invocation; no wgm journey recorded.

harnesses.name: OpenCode

skill_discovery.notes: OpenCode documents a native skill tool with project-local walk-up discovery plus Claude- and agent-compatible directories, including ~/.agents/skills.

invocation.notes: `opencode run` is documented as the non-interactive entry point. The permission and plugin flags needed for unattended tool use are version-dependent and unverified here — do not copy a flag set from this file into an autonomous run without checking it.

subagents.notes: OpenCode documents primary and subagent modes; wgm ships no OpenCode-format agent definitions, so dispatch is the operator's to wire.

harnesses.fallback: Inline sequential two-pass review per references/subagents.md.

adapter.notes: No OpenCode-format role definitions ship with wgm.

harnesses.notes: Skill discovery is unusually well documented; the flag surface for unattended runs is the unverified part.

harnesses.name: Aider

skill_discovery.notes: No Agent Skills discovery directory is documented at aider.chat as of 2026-08-24. This is an absence of documentation, not a vendor denial; third-party aggregator pages claiming native SKILL.md support in Aider were not corroborated by the vendor's own docs.

invocation.notes: Aider documents scripting via --message/-m, which sends one message and exits. wgm's own loop already lists aider among the CLIs it probes for a non-interactive mode.

subagents.notes: No dispatchable subagent primitive is documented.

harnesses.missing_capability: Agent Skills discovery (no directory scan) and host-dispatched subagents.
harnesses.fallback: Load the protocol explicitly instead of relying on discovery — `aider --read ~/.agents/skills/wgm/SKILL.md --message "..."`, the same habit as Aider's documented conventions file — and run both review passes inline. The deterministic gates still provide the backpressure.

adapter.notes: Making wgm discoverable here means an explicit --read of SKILL.md, or a wrapper that injects it; neither ships.

harnesses.notes: The clearest example of the portable kernel surviving a host that lacks the skill layer: the protocol is still text a model can be handed explicitly.

harnesses.name: Windsurf (Cascade)

skill_discovery.notes: Windsurf's Cascade documentation describes Agent Skills discovery including ~/.agents/skills. The positive is documented; wgm has verified none of it.

invocation.notes: No non-interactive invocation contract for an unattended wgm loop was corroborated on 2026-08-24. Absence of a corroborated headless mode is not proof that none exists.

harnesses.fallback: Use Windsurf interactively for the skill itself and drive scripts/loop.sh from a harness with a corroborated non-interactive mode.

adapter.notes: Nothing to adapt until the invocation contract is established.

harnesses.notes: Carried in the table precisely because it is Unknown: an unlisted harness looks like an oversight, while an Unknown one is a falsifiable statement about what wgm does not know.
